english.heading: Small Livestock Integration
body: Small livestock integration turns chickens, ducks, and bees into working parts of the farm.
Learn how animals can control pests, build fertility, support pollination, and return value to the soil.
Use the system you already have: food, manure, flowers, grazing, and careful movement across the land.

heading.text: U Ṱanganyisa Zwifuwo Zwiṱuku

body.text: U ṱanganyisa zwifuwo zwiṱuku hu ita uri dzikhuhu (chickens), dakisi (ducks) na dziṋotshi (bees) dzi vhe zwipiḓa zwi shumaho zwa bulasi.
body.backTranslation: Integrating small livestock makes chickens (chickens), ducks (ducks) and bees (bees) become working parts of the farm.

body.text: Gudani uri zwifuwo zwi nga langa hani pests, zwa engedza fertility, zwa thusa pollination, na u vhuyisa ndeme kha mavu.
body.backTranslation: Learn how livestock can manage pests, they increase fertility, they help pollination, and to return importance to the soil.

body.text: Shumisani system ine na vha nayo kale: zwiḽiwa, manure, maluvha, u ḽisa (grazing), na u sudzulusa zwifuwo nga ṱhogomelo kha mavu oṱhe.
body.backTranslation: Use the system that you already have: feed, manure, flowers, grazing (grazing), and moving livestock with care over all the soil.

english.heading: Why This Matters
body: Small livestock can do work beyond producing meat, eggs, or honey.
Chickens eat some insects and weed seeds. Their manure can become compost.
Ducks scratch less than chickens, but can still damage plants.
Bees and other pollinators help many crops. Each animal still needs suitable food, water, shelter and care.

heading.text: Ndi Ngani Izwi Zwi na Ndeme

body.text: Zwifuwo zwiṱuku zwi nga ita mushumo u fhiraho u bveledza nama, makumba kana mutoli (honey).
body.backTranslation: Small livestock can do a job beyond producing meat, eggs or honey (honey).

body.text: Dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi ḽa zwiṅwe zwikhokhonono (insects) na dziṅwe mbeu dza weeds. Manure yadzo i nga vha compost.
body.backTranslation: Chickens (chickens) eat some insects (insects) and some weed (weeds) seeds. Their manure may become compost.

body.text: Dakisi (ducks) dzi pala fhasi zwiṱuku u fhira dzikhuhu, fhedzi dzi nga kha ḓi tshinya zwimela.
body.backTranslation: Ducks (ducks) scratch the ground less than chickens, but they may still damage plants.

body.text: Dziṋotshi (bees) na zwiṅwe pollinators zwi thusa zwilimiwa zwinzhi. Tshifuwo tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tshi kha ḓi ṱoḓa zwiḽiwa zwo teaho, maḓi, vhudzulo na u ṱhogomelwa.
body.backTranslation: Bees (bees) and other pollinators help many crops. Each and every animal still needs suitable food, water, dwelling and being cared for.

english.heading: Learning Outcomes
body: By the end of this module, you will understand how chickens, ducks, bees, and guinea fowl fit into a working system.
You will know when chickens help a bed, and when their scratching can cause damage.
You will understand pollination, hive placement, and how livestock move nutrients around a farm.

heading.text: Zwine Na Ḓo Guda

body.text: Mafheleloni a ngudo iyi, ni ḓo pfesesa nḓila ine dzikhuhu (chickens), dakisi (ducks), dziṋotshi (bees) na guinea fowl dza vha ngayo tshipiḓa tsha system i shumaho.
body.backTranslation: At the end of this lesson, you will understand the way chickens (chickens), ducks (ducks), bees (bees) and guinea fowl (guinea fowl) become part of a working system.

body.text: Ni ḓo ḓivha musi dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi tshi thusa bede ḽa tsimu (garden bed), na musi u pala hadzo hu tshi nga tshinya.
body.backTranslation: You will know when chickens (chickens) help a garden bed (garden bed), and when their scratching may damage.

body.text: Ni ḓo pfesesa pollination, u vhea hive, na nḓila ine zwifuwo zwa tshimbidza ngayo nutrients kha bulasi.
body.backTranslation: You will understand pollination, to place hive, and the way in which livestock move nutrients on the farm.

english.heading: Watch: Hens Foraging After Harvest
body: Watch the hens peck at the ground among dry plant remains.
Chickens may eat some insects and weed seeds. They still need balanced feed, clean water and shelter.
Keep them away from seedlings and food ready to harvest.

heading.text: Sedzani: Dzikhuhu dzi tshi Ḽa Murahu ha Khaṋo

body.text: Lavhelesani dzikhuhu dzi tshi ṱoḓa zwiḽiwa fhasi vhukati ha zwo salaho zwa zwimela zwo omaho.
body.backTranslation: Watch chickens looking for food on the ground among the remains of dry plants.

body.text: Dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi nga ḽa zwiṅwe zwikhokhonono (insects) na dziṅwe mbeu dza weeds. Dzi kha ḓi ṱoḓa zwiḽiwa zwi fanelaho (balanced feed), maḓi o kunaho na vhudzulo.
body.backTranslation: Chickens (chickens) may eat some insects (insects) and some weed (weeds) seeds. They still need balanced feed (balanced feed), clean water and space.

body.text: Thivhelani dzikhuhu u swika kha seedlings na zwiḽiwa zwo lugelaho u kuvhanganywa.
body.backTranslation: Keep chickens away from seedlings (seedlings) and from food that is ready to be gathered.

english.heading: Chickens Turn Scratching Into Useful Work
body: Chickens can help an empty bed after harvest.
They scratch through plant remains and eat some insects and weed seeds.
Their manure and bedding can be composted and returned to the soil.
Foraging does not replace a balanced diet, clean water, shelter or daily care.

heading.text: U Pala ha Dzikhuhu hu Vha Mushumo u Thusaho

body.text: Dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi nga thusa bede ḽi si na zwilimiwa murahu ha khaṋo.
body.backTranslation: Chickens (chickens) may help a bed that has no crops after harvest.

body.text: Dzi pala fhasi kha zwo salaho zwa zwimela nahone dzi ḽa zwiṅwe zwikhokhonono (insects) na dziṅwe mbeu dza weeds.
body.backTranslation: They scratch the ground among plant remains and eat some insects (insects) and some weed (weeds) seeds.

body.text: Manure yadzo na bedding zwi nga itwa compost nahone zwa vhuyiswa kha mavu.
body.backTranslation: Their manure (manure) and bedding (bedding) can be made into compost (compost) and returned to the soil.

body.text: U ḓiṱoḓela zwiḽiwa a hu dzhii fhethu ha zwiḽiwa zwi fanelaho (balanced diet), maḓi o kunaho, vhudzulo kana u londwa ḓuvha na ḓuvha.
body.backTranslation: Foraging for themselves does not replace a balanced diet (balanced diet), clean water, shelter or daily care.

english.heading: Use Chickens at the Right Time
body: Use chickens in an empty bed after harvest.
Keep them away from seedlings and crops being harvested for food.
Fresh manure can carry germs. Ask an extension adviser how to manage manure safely before the next crop.
Move the birds before they damage the ground.

heading.text: Shumisani Dzikhuhu nga Tshifhinga Tsho Teaho
heading.backTranslation: Use Chickens at the Right Time

body.text: Shumisani dzikhuhu (chickens) kha bede ḽi si na zwilimiwa murahu ha khaṋo.
body.backTranslation: Use chickens (chickens) in a bed that has no crops after harvest.

body.text: Thivhelani dzikhuhu u swika kha seedlings na zwilimiwa zwine zwa khou kuvhanganywa u itela zwiḽiwa.
body.backTranslation: Keep chickens away from seedlings (seedlings) and from crops that are being gathered for food.

body.text: Manure ntswa i nga vha na germs. Vhudzisani extension adviser nḓila ya u langa manure nga tsireledzo phanḓa ha zwilimiwa zwi tevhelaho.
body.backTranslation: Fresh manure may have germs (germs). Ask an extension adviser (extension adviser) how to manage manure safely before the following crops.

body.text: Sudzulusani zwiṋoni phanḓa ha uri zwi tshinye mavu.
body.backTranslation: Move the birds before they finish/eat down the soil/ground.

english.heading: Ducks Suit Established Understorey
body: Ducks eat slugs and snails without the heavy scratching of chickens.
They may suit an established food forest understorey.
They can still eat or trample plants and make wet ground muddy. Watch the birds and move them when needed.
Provide clean water and suitable feed; foraging alone may not be enough.

heading.text: Dakisi Dzi Fanela Understorey yo no Aluwaho

body.text: Dakisi (ducks) dzi ḽa slugs na snails hu si na u pala fhasi nga maanḓa sa dzikhuhu.
body.backTranslation: Ducks (ducks) eat slugs (slugs) and snails (snails) without scratching the ground much like chickens.

body.text: Dzi nga fanela understorey ya food forest yo no aluwaho.
body.backTranslation: They may suit the understorey (understorey) of an established food forest (food forest).

body.text: Dzi nga kha ḓi ḽa zwimela kana u tshimbila nṱha hazwo (trample), na u ita uri mavu a re na maḓi (wet) a vhe matope. Lavhelesani zwiṋoni ni zwi sudzuluse musi zwi tshi ṱoḓea.
body.backTranslation: They may still eat plants or walk over them (trample), and make wet (wet) soil become mud. Watch the birds and move them when needed.

body.text: Ṋeani maḓi o kunaho na zwiḽiwa zwo teaho; u ḓiṱoḓela zwiḽiwa fhedzi hu nga vha hu sa ḓadzi ṱhoḓea dzadzo.
body.backTranslation: Give clean water and suitable feed; foraging for themselves alone may not meet their needs.

english.heading: Rotate the Tractor Across the Plot
body: A chicken tractor is a moveable, floorless pen.
Move it before the ground becomes bare, muddy or heavily covered with manure.
The right time depends on the birds, soil and weather. Let the ground recover between visits.
There is no single number of chickens that guarantees enough fertility for every plot.

heading.text: Sudzulusani Tractor kha Plot Yoṱhe
heading.backTranslation: Move the Tractor Over the Whole Plot

body.text: Chicken tractor ndi pen ine ya nga sudzuluswa, i si na fhasi (floorless).
body.backTranslation: A chicken tractor (Chicken tractor) is a pen (pen) that can be moved, with no floor (floorless).

body.text: Ni i sudzuluse phanḓa ha uri mavu a sale a si na tshithu (bare), a vhe na matope kana a fukedzwe nga manure nnzhi.
body.backTranslation: Move it before the soil is left bare (bare), becomes mud or is covered with a lot of manure (manure).

body.text: Tshifhinga tsho teaho tshi ya nga zwiṋoni, mavu na mutsho (weather). Litshani mavu a fhole phanḓa ha u vhuyisa zwiṋoni hafhu.
body.backTranslation: The right time depends on the birds, the soil and the weather (weather). Let the soil heal before bringing the birds back again.

body.text: A hu na nomboro nthihi ya dzikhuhu (chickens) ine ya fulufhedzisa fertility i ḓadzaho ṱhoḓea dza plot iṅwe na iṅwe.
body.backTranslation: There is no single number of chickens (chickens) that guarantees fertility (fertility) that meets the needs of every plot (plot).

english.heading: Watch: A Bee Moves Between Two Blossoms
body: Watch one bee move from one blossom to another.
Bees can carry pollen as they visit flowers.

heading.text: Sedzani: Ṋotshi i Bva kha Luvha i Ya kha Ḽiṅwe
heading.backTranslation: Watch: A Bee Goes from One Flower to Another

body.text: Lavhelesani ṋotshi nthihi i tshi bva kha luvha ḽithihi i tshi ya kha ḽiṅwe.
body.backTranslation: Watch one bee leaving one flower and going to another.

body.text: Dziṋotshi (bees) dzi nga hwala pollen musi dzi tshi dalela maluvha.
body.backTranslation: Bees (bees) can carry pollen when they visit flowers.

english.heading: Bees Help Pollinate Many Crops
body: Honeybees and other insects carry pollen between flowers.
This helps many fruit and vegetable crops, including avocado. Different crops and varieties have different pollination needs.
A hive does not guarantee higher yields everywhere. Weather, water, plant health and other pollinators also matter.

heading.text: Dziṋotshi Dzi Thusa Pollination ya Zwilimiwa Zwinzhi
heading.backTranslation: Bees Help Pollination of Many Crops

body.text: Dziṋotshi (honeybees) na zwiṅwe zwikhokhonono zwi hwala pollen vhukati ha maluvha.
body.backTranslation: Bees (honeybees) and other insects carry pollen between flowers.

body.text: Izwi zwi thusa zwilimiwa zwinzhi zwa mitshelo na miroho, zwi katela avocado. Zwilimiwa zwo fhambanaho na varieties dzo fhambanaho zwi na ṱhoḓea dzo fhambanaho dza pollination.
body.backTranslation: These help many crops of fruits and vegetables, they include avocado. Crops that are different and varieties that are different have different needs of pollination.

body.text: Hive a i fulufhedzisi khaṋo (yields) i engedzeaho fhethu hoṱhe. Mutsho (weather), maḓi, mutakalo wa zwimela na zwiṅwe pollinators zwi na ndeme na zwone.
body.backTranslation: A hive does not promise khaṋo (yields) that increases everywhere. Mutsho (weather), water, health of plants and other pollinators have importance too.

english.heading: South Africa’s Native Honeybees
body: South Africa has two native honeybee subspecies.
The Cape honeybee is found in the Western Cape and parts of the Eastern Cape. The African honeybee is native to central and most of southern Africa.
These broad natural ranges are not a guide for moving bees. The Department's control measures set a demarcation line for bee movement. Check current rules before moving bees or hives.

heading.text: Dziṋotshi dza Mupo dza Afrika Tshipembe

body.text: Afrika Tshipembe i na subspecies mbili dza ṋotshi (honeybee) dza mupo.
body.backTranslation: South Africa has two subspecies of bee (honeybee) of nature.

body.text: Cape honeybee i wanala kha Western Cape na kha zwiṅwe zwipiḓa zwa Eastern Cape. African honeybee ndi ya mupo kha Afrika ya vhukati na vhunzhi ha Afrika ya Tshipembe (southern Africa).
body.backTranslation: The Cape honeybee (Cape honeybee) is found in the Western Cape and in some parts of the Eastern Cape. The African honeybee (African honeybee) is natural in central Africa and most of southern Africa (southern Africa).

body.text: Fhethu hu hulwane hune dza dzula hone nga mupo a hu sumbedzi uri dziṋotshi dzi nga sudzuluswa ngafhi. Control measures dza Muhasho (the Department) dzi vhea demarcation line ya u sudzuluswa ha dziṋotshi. Sedzani milayo ya zwino phanḓa ha u sudzulusa dziṋotshi kana hives.
body.backTranslation: The large area where they live naturally does not show where bees may be moved. The Department's (the Department) control measures (Control measures) set a demarcation line (demarcation line) for moving bees. Check the current rules before moving bees or hives (hives).

english.heading: Place the Hive With Care
body: Learn from an experienced local beekeeper before getting a hive.
Keep hives away from busy paths, homes and places where children play.
Morning sun can help, but a safe location comes first.
Plan how people and animals will move around the site.

heading.text: Vheani Hive nga Ṱhogomelo

body.text: Gudani kha beekeeper wa fhethu ane a vha na vhukoni ha tshifhinga tshilapfu phanḓa ha u wana hive.
body.backTranslation: Learn from a local beekeeper (beekeeper) who has long-time ability before getting a hive (hive).

body.text: Vheani hives kule na nḓila dzo dalaho, mahaya na fhethu hune vhana vha tamba hone.
body.backTranslation: Place hives (hives) far from busy roads, homesteads and places where children play.

body.text: Ḓuvha ḽa matsheloni ḽi nga thusa, fhedzi fhethu ha tsireledzo hu tou thoma.
body.backTranslation: Afternoon sun may help, but a safe place comes first.

body.text: Pulanani uri vhathu na zwifuwo zwi ḓo tshimbila hani fhethu henefho.
body.backTranslation: Plan how people and livestock will walk in that place.

english.heading: Strong Colonies Need Care and Flowers
body: Provide flowering plants through the seasons and avoid exposing bees to pesticides.
Active bees do not prove that the farm is free of chemicals or disease.

Registration is required for activities defined by the national honey-bee control measures. These include keeping managed hives for bee products, queen rearing, commercial pollination, and removing, eradicating or relocating colonies. Check with the Department if you are unsure whether your activity is covered.
If a colony swarms repeatedly, ask a trained beekeeper to inspect it. Crowding is one possible cause, not a diagnosis.

heading.text: Colony i Khwaṱhaho i Ṱoḓa Ṱhogomelo na Maluvha
heading.backTranslation: A Strong Colony Needs Care and Flowers

body.text: Vhani na zwimela zwi re na maluvha nga zwifhinga zwoṱhe zwa ṅwaha nahone ni tsireledze dziṋotshi (bees) kha pesticides.
body.backTranslation: Have plants with flowers at all times of the year and protect the bees (bees) from pesticides (pesticides).

body.text: Dziṋotshi dzi tshi khou shuma a dzi khwaṱhisedzi uri bulasi ḽi si na chemicals kana vhulwadze.
body.backTranslation: Working bees do not guarantee that the farm has no chemicals (chemicals) or disease.

body.text: Registration i a ṱoḓea kha zwiito zwo ṱalutshedzwaho nga national honey-bee control measures. Izwi zwi katela u fuwa hives dzo langwaho u itela zwibveledzwa zwa dziṋotshi, queen rearing, commercial pollination, na u bvisa, u fhelisa kana u sudzulusa colonies. Vhudzisani Muhasho (the Department) arali ni sa ḓivhi uri tshiito tshaṋu tshi a katelwa.
body.backTranslation: Registration (Registration) is required for activities specified by the national honey-bee control measures (national honey-bee control measures). These include keeping managed hives (hives) for bee products, queen rearing (queen rearing), commercial pollination (commercial pollination), and removing, destroying or moving colonies (colonies). Ask the Department (the Department) if you do not know whether your activity is included.

body.text: Arali colony i tshi ita swarm hafhu na hafhu, humbelani beekeeper o gudiswaho u i sedzesa. Crowding ndi tshiṅwe tsha zwiitisi zwine zwa nga vha hone, a si diagnosis.
body.backTranslation: If a colony swarms again and again, ask for a beekeeper who has been taught to look closely at it. Crowding is one of the causes that may be there; it is not a diagnosis.

english.heading: Nutrients Moving Through the Farm
body: Some nutrients move from plants to animals. Bought feed also brings nutrients into the farm. Some nutrients may return to the growing area through compost made from manure. Food and other products carry nutrients away.

heading.text: Nutrients dzi Tshimbilaho kha Bulasi

body.text: Dziṅwe nutrients dzi bva kha zwimela dza ya kha zwifuwo. Zwiḽiwa zwa zwifuwo zwo rengwaho na zwone zwi ḓisa nutrients kha bulasi. Dziṅwe nutrients dzi nga vhuya kha fhethu ha u lima nga compost yo itwaho nga manure. Zwiḽiwa na zwiṅwe zwibveledzwa zwi dzhia nutrients zwi tshi bva.
body.backTranslation: Some nutrients (nutrients) go from plants to livestock. Bought livestock feed also brings nutrients to the farm. Some nutrients may return to the growing place through compost (compost) made from manure (manure). Food and other products take nutrients away when they leave.

english.heading: Some Nutrients Return; Others Enter and Leave
body: Animals can return some nutrients through compost made from manure. Fresh manure can carry harmful germs. Compost manure fully before using it around food crops.
Chickens eat suitable farm produce and insects.
Bought feed brings nutrients into the farm. Food sold or taken home and other products carry nutrients away. Keep track of feed bought in and food sold or taken home.
Scraps alone may not meet the animals’ needs.

heading.text: Dziṅwe Dzi Vhuya; Dziṅwe Dzi Dzhena na u Bva
heading.backTranslation: Some Return; Some Come In and Go Out

body.text: Zwifuwo zwi nga vhuyisa dziṅwe nutrients nga compost yo itwaho nga manure. Manure ntswa i nga vha na germs dzi vhaisaho. Itani compost ya manure zwo fhelelaho phanḓa ha u i shumisa tsini ha zwilimiwa zwa zwiḽiwa.
body.backTranslation: Livestock may return some nutrients (nutrients) through compost (compost) made from manure (manure). Fresh manure may have harmful germs (germs). Fully compost manure before using it near food crops.

body.text: Dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi ḽa zwibveledzwa zwa bulasi zwo teaho na zwikhokhonono (insects).
body.backTranslation: Chickens (chickens) eat suitable farm products and insects (insects).

body.text: Zwiḽiwa zwa zwifuwo zwo rengwaho zwi ḓisa nutrients kha bulasi. Zwiḽiwa zwo rengiswaho kana zwo dzhiiwaho hayani na zwiṅwe zwibveledzwa zwi dzhia nutrients zwi tshi bva. Ṅwalani zwiḽiwa zwa zwifuwo zwo rengwaho na zwiḽiwa zwo rengiswaho kana zwo dzhiiwaho hayani.
body.backTranslation: Bought livestock feed brings nutrients (nutrients) to the farm. Food that is sold or taken home and other products take nutrients away when they leave. Write down the bought livestock feed and the food that is sold or taken home.

body.text: Zwo salaho zwa zwiḽiwa fhedzi zwi nga vha zwi sa ḓadzi ṱhoḓea dza zwifuwo.
body.backTranslation: Leftovers of food alone may not meet the needs of livestock.

english.heading: Guinea Fowl Forage, but Health Checks Still Matter
body: Guinea fowl forage for insects and may eat ticks.
Do not rely on them to protect people or livestock from ticks or tick-borne disease.
Keep checking animals and follow a local animal-health plan.
Foraging birds are one part of the farm, not a replacement for health care.

heading.text: Guinea Fowl dzi Ḓiṱoḓela, fhedzi Sedzani Mutakalo
heading.backTranslation: Guinea Fowl seek for themselves (fend for themselves), but Check Health

body.text: Guinea fowl dzi ḓiṱoḓela zwikhokhonono (insects) nahone dzi nga ḽa ticks.
body.backTranslation: Guinea fowl (Guinea fowl) forage for themselves insects (insects) and may eat ticks (ticks).

body.text: Ni songo ḓitika ngadzo u tsireledza vhathu kana zwifuwo (livestock) kha ticks kana vhulwadze vhu ḓiswaho nga ticks.
body.backTranslation: Do not rely on them to protect people or livestock (livestock) from ticks (ticks) or from disease brought by ticks.

body.text: Dzulani ni tshi sedza zwifuwo nahone ni tevhele animal-health plan ya fhethu.
body.backTranslation: Keep watching the livestock and follow the local animal-health plan (animal-health plan).

body.text: Zwiṋoni zwi ḓiṱoḓelaho zwiḽiwa ndi tshipiḓa tshithihi tsha bulasi; a zwi dzhii fhethu ha u ṱhogomela mutakalo.
body.backTranslation: Birds that forage for themselves are one part of the farm; they do not replace caring for health.

english.heading: Ask Three Questions for Every Animal
body: For each animal, ask what it can eat here.
Ask what useful things it produces.
Then ask what else it needs. Include water, suitable feed, shelter, fencing and daily care.
Some needs may require bought inputs. Plan for them before bringing animals onto the land.

heading.text: Mbudziso Tharu kha Tshifuwo Tshiṅwe na Tshiṅwe

body.text: Kha tshifuwo tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe, vhudzisani uri tshi nga ḽa mini fhano.
body.backTranslation: For each animal, ask what it could eat here.

body.text: Vhudzisani uri tshi bveledza zwithu zwifhio zwi thusaho.
body.backTranslation: Ask what helpful things it produces.

body.text: Nga murahu vhudzisani uri ndi zwifhio zwiṅwe zwine tsha zwi ṱoḓa. Katelani maḓi, zwiḽiwa zwa zwifuwo zwo teaho, vhudzulo, fencing na u londwa ḓuvha na ḓuvha.
body.backTranslation: Afterwards ask what else it needs. Include water, suitable livestock feed, space, fencing (fencing) and daily care.

body.text: Dziṅwe ṱhoḓea dzi nga ṱoḓa inputs dzo rengwaho. Pulanani nga hazwo phanḓa ha u ḓisa zwifuwo kha mavu.
body.backTranslation: Some needs may require bought inputs (inputs). Plan for them before bringing livestock onto the land.

english.heading: Grazing and Goat Worm Control
body: Chickens following goats are not a proven replacement for goat worm control.
Grazing management can help, but goats still need health checks.
Work with a veterinary or animal-health adviser on a parasite plan for your herd.
Do not stop treatment because chickens have visited the grazing camp.

heading.text: U Ḽisa na u Langa Zwivhungu zwa Mbudzi

body.text: Dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi tevhelaho mbudzi (goats) a si nḓila yo khwaṱhisedzwaho ya u dzhia fhethu ha u langa zwivhungu (worms) zwa mbudzi.
body.backTranslation: Chickens (chickens) that follow goats (goats) are not a reliable way to replace controlling goat worms (worms).

body.text: U langa u ḽisa (grazing management) hu nga thusa, fhedzi mbudzi dzi kha ḓi ṱoḓa u sedzwa mutakalo.
body.backTranslation: Managing grazing (grazing management) may help, but goats still need health checks.

body.text: Shumani na veterinary kana animal-health adviser kha parasite plan ya tshigwada tshaṋu.
body.backTranslation: Work with a veterinary or animal-health adviser (animal-health adviser) on a parasite plan (parasite plan) for your herd.

body.text: Ni songo litsha u alafha ngauri dzikhuhu dzo dalela fhethu ha u ḽisa (grazing camp).
body.backTranslation: Do not stop treating because chickens have visited the grazing camp (grazing camp).

english.heading: Field Assignment: Draw Where Resources Go
body: Walk your smallholding and choose an area where livestock could support another part of the system.
Record what food, scraps, pests, surplus produce, manure, or flowering resources are already present.
Then note what each animal could produce, and what it would need from the farm.
Draw one useful link between livestock and the rest of your farm. Show what comes in and what leaves.

heading.text: Mushumo wa Tsimu: Olani Hune Zwiko zwa Ya Hone
heading.backTranslation: Field Task: Draw Where Resources Go

body.text: Tshimbilani kha smallholding yaṋu ni nange fhethu hune zwifuwo zwa nga thusa tshiṅwe tshipiḓa tsha system.
body.backTranslation: Walk around your smallholding (smallholding) and choose places where livestock could help another part of the system (system).

body.text: Ṅwalani zwiḽiwa, zwo salaho zwa zwiḽiwa, pests, zwibveledzwa zwi fhiraho zwine na zwi ṱoḓa (surplus), manure kana zwimela zwi re na maluvha zwo no vha hone.
body.backTranslation: Write down feed, feed leftovers, pests (pests), products beyond what you need (surplus), manure (manure) or flowering plants that are already there.

body.text: Nga murahu ṅwalani zwine tshifuwo tshiṅwe na tshiṅwe tsha nga zwi bveledza, na zwine tsha nga zwi ṱoḓa kha bulasi.
body.backTranslation: Afterwards write down what each animal could produce, and what it could need on the farm.

body.text: Olani vhushaka (link) vhuthihi vhu thusaho vhukati ha zwifuwo na zwiṅwe zwipiḓa zwa bulasi ḽaṋu. Sumbedzani zwi dzhenaho na zwi bvaho.
body.backTranslation: Draw one helpful link (link) between livestock and other parts of your farm. Show what goes in and what goes out.

english.heading: Field Action: Put One Link to Work
body: Choose one safe action from this module.
Plan how chickens could use an empty bed after harvest, ask a beekeeper about a safe hive position, or check your animals’ daily needs.
Record the food, water, shelter and care that the action requires.
Start with the resources and help you can reliably provide.

heading.text: Tshiito tsha Tsimu: Shumisani Vhushaka Vhuthihi

body.text: Nangani tshiito tshithihi tshi tsireledzeaho kha ngudo iyi.
body.backTranslation: Choose one safe activity from this lesson.

body.text: Pulanani uri dzikhuhu (chickens) dzi nga shumisa hani bede ḽi si na zwilimiwa murahu ha khaṋo, vhudzisani beekeeper nga ha fhethu ha tsireledzo ha hive, kana ni sedze ṱhoḓea dza ḓuvha na ḓuvha dza zwifuwo zwaṋu.
body.backTranslation: Plan how chickens (chickens) could use a bed that has no crops after harvest, ask a beekeeper (beekeeper) about a safe place for a hive (hive), or check the daily needs of your livestock.

body.text: Ṅwalani zwiḽiwa, maḓi, vhudzulo na u ṱhogomela zwine tshiito itsho tsha zwi ṱoḓa.
body.backTranslation: Write down the feed, water, space and care that the activity needs.

body.text: Thomani nga zwiko na thuso zwine na nga zwi ṋea nga nḓila i fulufhedzeaho.
body.backTranslation: Start with the resources and help that you could give in a reliable way.
